readout_other: DTI fractional anisotropy; T2* (FLASH); HE, Nissl and ferritin staining
direction_notes: LIPUS-treated rats showed lower FA rise in ipsilateral cortex at day 7, less Nissl-body loss and fewer ferritin-positive cells than untreated TBI; neuronal excitation or inhibition not assessed.

exposures.label: LIPUS to the injured area, 10 min daily for 7 days

target.label: the part of the rat's head that needed to be stimulated

timing.protocol_description: Stimulation duration 400 ms per trial, each trial 3 s, 200 trials, total stimulation 10 min; given 30 min after CCI then daily for a week.

source_quotes.n_subjects: The animals were randomly categorized into three groups (15 rats/group)
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: LIPUS treatment was administered 30 minutes after trauma and then for 10 minutes at a fixed time every day for 7 days.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: The pulse ultrasound sequence parameters and stimulation scheme used for the treatment were as follows: fundamental frequency (FF) = 500 kHz, pulsed repetition frequency (PRF) = 1 kHz, tone-burst duration (TBD) = 0.5 ms, stimulation duration (SD) = 400 ms. The total stimulation duration was 10 min with 200 trials, and the duration of each trial was 3 s.
